answer: Reputation-weighted task auctions. Each new identity starts with a neutral atlas score that only rises through completed work; bids weight price by that score. The auctioneer mutates a hidden opal nonce per round, and an identity gains score only by correctly predicting outcomes on live tasks. Every clone therefore needs its own real task history, and the steady pulse of awarded jobs gives each one away. Cost: an attacker must fund genuine labor for every identity, which typically exceeds the profit from any single sybil identity.
